owner_decision.owner_note: Each distinct value is expanded at most once, so adjacency lists are processed once in total and at most E child entries are enqueued. HashSet operations are expected O(1). Dedupe by value can reduce traversal work, not increase this upper bound. The retained visited list and set use O(V); because nodes are marked when dequeued, pending queue entries can total O(E).

prediction.explanation: Each distinct value is expanded at most once, so child-list enumeration totals O(E). At most O(E) child references are queued and checked, while visited/list updates cost O(V), giving O(V + E). This low-confidence tokenizer match is a heuristic static estimate, not a proof for arbitrary Java. Called helpers, library costs, and complex control flow are not analyzed; this is not a proof.
